page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on Intel x86_64 architecture. The server provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 128 GB of RAM, establishing a compute-dense ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel execution and mathematical throughput. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, leading to top-tier performance in image processing and database operation tests. Compiling software with Clang, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput all register in the upper quartile of benchmarked machines. In-memory transaction benchmarks demonstrate high efficiency, recording 71.84 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:2 core-to-memory ratio delivers cost-effective compute capacity for calculation-heavy workloads that do not demand extensive RAM pools. However, memory-intensive processes and high-throughput local disk caching are constrained by the absence of local storage and the 2 GB per core allocation. The n4-highcpu-64 is well suited for continuous integration pipelines, software compilation suites, batch media processing, CPU-based machine learning inference, and computational microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-oriented virtual server engineered on Intel x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 128 GB of system memory. Operating at a 2 GB per vCPU allocation, the instance delivers high compute density for compute-bound applications without the overhead of excess memory. Hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets drives strong performance in integer math, image manipulation, software compilation, and vector operations, alongside upper-quartile results in static web throughput and Redis operations. The platform excludes local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs, utilizing network-attached block storage for disk operations. This profile yields efficient multi-threaded throughput and high instruction concurrency, making the instance an effective fit for software build pipelines, batch data transformations, media rendering, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
